request: A reader gives a date and wants each country's head on that day.
A country whose office was vacant is absent; on a handover day, the day one term ends and the next begins, both heads show.
A reader pages through a country's list ten terms at a time, first to latest, and asks for the second page.
term_start is distinct within a country (HOG_HEAD_I_18 checks it), so the order, and with it each page, is fixed.

changes.title: A term by its official number
request: A reader has a country and a term number, as the official list writes it, and wants that term.
The number need not be unique: where a person keeps one number on each term (HOG_OFFICE_B_03), it gives every term of that person, earliest first.
changes.sql:
SELECT *
FROM head
WHERE country = :country
  AND number = :number
ORDER BY term_start ASC

changes.title: Terms that end after the head died
request: A term cannot outlast its head.
List the terms whose end falls in a year after the head's death, by country, then in date order; the check passes when nothing comes back.
changes.sql:
SELECT *
FROM head
WHERE died IS NOT NULL
  AND CAST(SUBSTR(term_end, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) > died
ORDER BY country ASC, term_start ASC

SELECT *,
       CAST(julianday(COALESCE(term_end, date('now'))) - julianday(term_start) AS INTEGER) AS days
FROM head
WHERE country = :country
ORDER BY days DESC, term_start ASC

request: Per country, its first :n terms and its most recent :n, each row saying which it is.
A row is 'first' when it is among the first :n, so with a country of fewer than 2 * :n terms the two sets overlap and 'first' wins.
term_start is distinct within a country (HOG_HEAD_I_18 checks it), so the numbering has no ties.
changes.sql:
SELECT *,
       CASE WHEN first_rn <= :n THEN 'first' ELSE 'latest' END AS which
FROM (SELECT h.*,
             ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY term_start ASC)  AS first_rn,
             ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY term_start DESC) AS latest_rn
      FROM head AS h)
WHERE first_rn <= :n
   OR latest_rn <= :n
ORDER BY country ASC, term_start ASC

request: Per country, over the terms that have ended, each party's share of the days in office as a percentage of that country's total (its tenure share), the top three parties; a succession ('A/B') counts as a party of its own.
At a tie in days, by party.
changes.sql:
WITH totals AS (SELECT country,
                       party,
                       SUM(julianday(term_end) - julianday(term_start)) AS days
                FROM head
                WHERE term_end IS NOT NULL
                GROUP BY country, party),
     placed AS (SELECT *,
                       ROUND(100.0 * days / NULLIF(SUM(days) OVER (PARTITION BY country), 0), 1) AS tenure_share,
                       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY days DESC, party ASC)    AS place
                FROM totals)
SELECT country, party, tenure_share
FROM placed
WHERE place <= 3
ORDER BY country ASC, place ASC

changes.title: Repeated term starts
request: Several exercises rely on term_start being distinct within a country, which the schema does not declare.
List each country and start date held by more than one term, with how many, by country, then by date; the check passes when nothing comes back.
changes.sql:
SELECT country, term_start, COUNT(*) AS terms
FROM head
GROUP BY country, term_start
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY country ASC, term_start ASC

changes.title: More than one incumbent
request: A country has one head in office now, at most; HOG_OFFICE_I_03 checks the other side, an office with none.
List the countries with more than one term that has not ended, and how many; the check passes when nothing comes back.
changes.sql:
SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS open_terms
FROM head
WHERE term_end IS NULL
GROUP BY country
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY country ASC

SELECT *,
       CAST(julianday(term_start) - julianday(previous_term_end) AS INTEGER) - 1 AS days_vacant
FROM (SELECT h.*,
             LAG(name) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY term_start)     AS previous_name,
             LAG(term_end) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY term_start) AS previous_term_end
      FROM head AS h)
WHERE julianday(term_start) - julianday(previous_term_end) > 1
ORDER BY country ASC, term_start ASC

SELECT country, name, terms, days
FROM (SELECT country,
             name,
             COUNT(*)                                                                                 AS terms,
             CAST(SUM(julianday(COALESCE(term_end, date('now'))) - julianday(term_start)) AS INTEGER) AS days,
             RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY country
                 ORDER BY SUM(julianday(COALESCE(term_end, date('now'))) - julianday(term_start)) DESC) AS place
      FROM head
      GROUP BY country, name)
WHERE place = 1
ORDER BY country ASC

WITH ordered AS (SELECT country,
                        party,
                        term_start,
                        term_end,
                        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY term_start)        AS seq,
                        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country, party ORDER BY term_start) AS seq_in_party
                 FROM head),
     runs AS (SELECT country,
                     party,
                     COUNT(*)                             AS terms,
                     MIN(term_start)                      AS since,
                     MAX(COALESCE(term_end, date('now'))) AS until
              FROM ordered
              GROUP BY country, party, seq - seq_in_party),
     placed AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY terms DESC, since ASC) AS place
                FROM runs)
SELECT country, party, terms, since, until
FROM placed
WHERE place = 1
ORDER BY country ASC

SELECT *
FROM (SELECT h.*,
             LAG(name) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY term_start)  AS predecessor,
             LEAD(name) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY term_start) AS successor
      FROM head AS h)
WHERE name = :name
ORDER BY country ASC, term_start ASC

request: Per office, with its title, how many of its heads are still living, the incumbent included, and 0 where none is, by country code.
A name is taken as one person within a country; the condition on died goes into the join, so an office without a living head still shows.
changes.sql:
SELECT g.*, COUNT(DISTINCT h.name) AS living
FROM office g
         LEFT JOIN head h ON h.country = g.country AND h.died IS NULL
GROUP BY g.country
ORDER BY g.country ASC

request: Per office, with its title, the terms begun in each century from the 18th to the 21st, one column per century, by country code.
A century is counted the way people say the 1800s, so 1800 is in the 19th, as in HOG_SCHEMA_A_06.
A SUM of CASE per column turns the rows of a GROUP BY into columns.
changes.sql:
SELECT g.*,
       SUM(CASE WHEN h.term_start >= '1700' AND h.term_start < '1800' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS c18,
       SUM(CASE WHEN h.term_start >= '1800' AND h.term_start < '1900' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS c19,
       SUM(CASE WHEN h.term_start >= '1900' AND h.term_start < '2000' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS c20,
       SUM(CASE WHEN h.term_start >= '2000' AND h.term_start < '2100' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS c21
FROM office g
         JOIN head h ON h.country = g.country
GROUP BY g.country
ORDER BY g.country ASC

request: A reader gives a date and wants every office with its head on that day, or '(vacant)' where the office was empty or the list had not yet begun.
On a handover day, the day one term ends and the next begins, both heads show.
changes.sql:
SELECT g.country, g.head_title, COALESCE(h.name, '(vacant)') AS name, h.number, h.term_start, h.term_end
FROM office g
         LEFT JOIN head h ON h.country = g.country
    AND h.term_start <= :date
    AND (h.term_end IS NULL OR h.term_end >= :date)
ORDER BY g.country ASC, h.term_start ASC NULLS FIRST

SELECT i.country    AS country,
       i.name       AS incumbent,
       i.term_start AS took_office,
       o.country    AS other_country,
       g.head_title AS other_title,
       o.name       AS other_head
FROM head i
         JOIN head o ON o.country <> i.country
    AND o.term_start <= i.term_start
    AND (o.term_end IS NULL OR o.term_end >= i.term_start)
         JOIN office g ON g.country = o.country
WHERE i.term_end IS NULL
ORDER BY i.country ASC, o.country ASC, o.term_start ASC
